text:
alex: quick heads up — failing smoke on local CI: TS SDK returns metadata in responses by default, but curl to the REST API does not. suspect serializer mismatch for the include_metadata flag.

maria: can you paste a minimal repro?

alex: yep — curl vs ts snippet below. when I call curl without include_metadata I get no metadata in response; SDK returns metadata unless I explicitly set includeMetadata: false.

curl:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small","input":"hi"}'
```

response headers/body show no metadata key.

TS SDK:
```
client.generate({ model: 'redwood-small', input: 'hi' })
// -> response includes `.metadata` object by default
```

sam: interesting. is the SDK adding includeMetadata=true on the wire or is the server default different by client type?

alex: looked at the recording in request-logs: SDK sends body {"include_metadata": true} because the serializer maps includeMetadata -> include_metadata and uses a client-side default true. REST examples/docs never said it defaults to true.

jordan: that feels like a breaking client-side behavior. docs say include_metadata is optional and server default should be false (no metadata unless requested).

maria: agreed — changing SDK default from true->false would be a behavioral change for customers who relied on metadata showing up. we need a migration plan.

alex: proposed flow: 1) fix SDK serializer to only emit include_metadata when explicitly set (no implicit true). 2) ship a patch release for python & ts that keeps existing behavior behind a feature flag or opt-out (so current users unaffected). 3) add a deprecation warning in the next minor when flag unset. 4) clean up in major.

sam: alternative smaller change: server could treat absent include_metadata as true for back-compat for N weeks, but that masks the root cause and keeps docs wrong. not ideal.

jordan: I can own an RFC note on compatibility windows. but we should prefer client-side fix + careful release notes.

maria: can you open two issues: one in sdk-js (serializer) and one in docs to clarify server default? tag me and @sam.

alex: created tickets: SDK-4578 (ts serializer only-emit-if-set) and DOCS-312 (clarify include_metadata default). linked PR draft for SDK change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/289

alex: minimal patch diff (sketch):
```
// current
const body = { include_metadata: options.includeMetadata ?? true }

// change
const body = {}
if (options.includeMetadata !== undefined) body.include_metadata = options.includeMetadata
```

deploy-bot: rolled out sdk-js@1.23.4-canary to staging at 2025-11-01T03:12:10Z :rocket:

sam: nice. timeline? if we fix serializer to not emit by default, we should release a patch that preserves previous behavior behind an env var like REDWOOD_SDK_EMIT_METADATA_BY_DEFAULT=true for one release cycle.

jordan: +1. we also need to audit other boolean flags that might be using `?? true` pattern — could be more surprises.

maria: I'll do a sweep in the docs and add a TODO list. alex/sam, can one of you do the audit in sdk-js for other flags?

alex: I can do a quick grep this afternoon and open follow-ups.

sam: I'll draft the release note bullet and the env var plan.

jordan: cool. let's aim to cut the patch tomorrow US morning. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks all — filing follow-ups now and I'll ping the PR once tests pass. :pray:
